subject: HSM handoff & cutover plan for Acme Payments KMS
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike@hsmvendor.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@acme-payments.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HSM handoff & cutover plan for Acme Payments KMS

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is our initial cutover play: a short checklist for network prechecks and firmware assurances that we'll need signed off before we move traffic to the new HSM-backed KMS endpoint.

High-level plan (proposed window):
- Staging rehearsal: 2026-08-10 02:00–04:00 UTC (non-prod)
- Production cutover: 2026-08-14 01:30–03:30 UTC (low-traffic)

Pre-reqs from Acme / Redwood network team:
- Whitelist management IPs (see connectivity-checklist.csv)
- TCP 443 and 8443 outbound from KMS host to HSM cluster management IPs
- Allow UDP 123 for NTP to HSM appliances
- Static egress IPs (no NAT) for HSM mgmt plane (we can provide ranges)

Security artifacts attached: hsm-cert-chain.pem, firmware-sig.pdf. We also have a hardware attestation report from our factory (can share on request).

Questions for the cutover runbook: do you have an existing KMS test credential we can use to validate signing/unseal during rehearsal? Also, acceptable rollback time SLA?

I'll stand up remote console access for the rehearsal and will provide a dedicated slack channel.

Regards,
Mike Turner
Principal Solutions Engineer
HSMVendor Inc.

Attachments: hsm-cert-chain.pem (pem), firmware-sig.pdf (pdf)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mike Turner <mike@hsmvendor.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HSM handoff & cutover plan for Acme Payments KMS

Mike — thanks, received. Quick clarifications before we circulate to Acme SecOps: 

1) Does the HSM expose PKCS#11 + a FIPS 140-3 validated crypto module? We need module cert details for procurement.
2) Firmware update during the window: will the firmware-sig.pdf trigger a mandatory reboot that would cause a >2m outage? We need a staging rehearsal to verify zero-or-minimal disruption to existing KMS calls.
3) For the management plane: is a VPN + static route sufficient or do you require BGP peering?

Action: Dylan — can you confirm whether our KMS hosts can be assigned static egress IPs without breaking cross-region routing? Monica — can you prepare a short acceptance checklist for the rehearsal focused on key unwrap/unwrap flows and token signing validation? Markus — please add a short rollback play (steps to re-point DNS and invalidate new KMS certs).

I'll aim to get Acme SecOps the answers by EOD and propose a 30-minute tabletop with their team on Thu.

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: Mike Turner <mike@hsmvendor.io>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HSM handoff & cutover plan for Acme Payments KMS

Hannah — answers inline: 

1) PKCS#11 + a FIPS 140-3 Level 2 boundary. Module cert: FIPS-2025-029 (see attestation-report-20260630.pdf attached).
2) Firmware update: the signed firmware will require a single HSM appliance reboot. With our HA pair, we expect handoff to sustain short spikes (under 30s) if the orchestration is sequenced correctly. No mandatory >2m outage in typical cases, but we recommend draining sessions and using prefix cache warming for KMS clients.
3) Management plane: VPN + static egress IPs is fine. BGP is optional for customers that run private interconnects. We will provide the management IP ranges in the connectivity-checklist.csv.

We can provision a short-lived test key and PKCS#11 token for the rehearsal; please provide an ssh public key for Ec2 host access.

Attaching: attestation-report-20260630.pdf, connectivity-checklist.csv.

Happy to join the tabletop on Thu.

Best,
Mike

Attachments: attestation-report-20260630.pdf (pdf), connectivity-checklist.csv (csv)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Mike Turner <mike@hsmvendor.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HSM handoff & cutover plan for Acme Payments KMS

Adding network constraints and acceptance tests from infra: 

- We can allocate static egress IPs from our NAT pool per AZ, but for the HSM management plane we prefer direct routed prefixes (no double NAT) for packet source stability in vendor ACLs. If vendor cannot accept NAT'd IPs, we'll request a direct egress path via the transit VPC.
- Firewall rules we will open for the rehearsal window: outbound TCP 443/8443 to vendor mgmt range, UDP 123 to vendor NTP endpoints, TCP 22 limited to the vendor console jump host only.
- Acceptance tests (staging rehearsal):
  * KMS seal/unseal cycle (10 iterations) with 95% success rate under 200ms median latency
  * PKCS#11 sign/verify for a 512B payload (compare signatures against vendor test vector)
  * TLS cert chain validation using hsm-cert-chain.pem (verify chain and timestamps)

Rollback notes: Have DNS TTL lowered to 60s 12 hours prior to cutover; keep previous KMS endpoint running for 30 minutes post-cutover and monitor error budget. If >1% client error for 5m, execute immediate rollback.

Mike — please confirm vendor test vectors and the exact management IP ranges so we can prep ACLs. Also send the ssh pubkey address for the test instance.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Staff Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Thanks everyone — summary & next steps: 

- Mike: please upload the vendor test vectors and management IP ranges to the Confluence doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/KB/ACME-HSM-CUTOVER-2026) and share the ssh key upload endpoint. Also confirm whether you can run the staging rehearsal with firmware disabled (we want to validate control-plane flows first).
- Dylan: prepare the transit VPC request and lower DNS TTL to 60s by 2026-08-13 12:00 UTC.
- Monica: assemble the staging acceptance checklist (10 iterations for seal/unseal) and create the monitoring dashboard (latency + error rate).
- Markus: draft the DNS rollback play and cert revocation steps; include the command snippets.

I've scheduled a 30-minute tabletop with Acme SecOps for Thu 2026-08-06 20:00 UTC (invite sent). We'll treat the tabletop as the gating review before the staging rehearsal.

If there are no blocking items from vendor attestation or our network team after the tabletop, we will proceed with rehearsal on 2026-08-10.
